newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary public sector accepts 17pct '97 pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Hungary public sector accepts 17pct '97 pay rise.

text.p: Hungary's public sector workers will receive a 17 percent gross pay increase next year after a Friday agreement between workers' representatives and government officials.

Hungarian news agency MTI reported that the 200,000-strong Health Workers' Union (EDDSZ) had accepted the proposed wage increase at the last minute, clearing the way for Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy and Labour Minister Peter Kiss to sign the document on behalf of the government.
Municipalities, however, did not join the agreement saying the pay rises cannot be financed.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn, who countersigned the agreement, said the government had fulfilled its public sector pay rise undertaking this year and guarantees to do the same in 1997.
The agreement is based on government inflation forecasts for next year.

Gyorgy Suranyi, the president of Hungary's central bank said on Thursday he expected year-on-year inflation to drop to 17 percent by December 1997 from an estimated 20 percent at the end of this month, and average annual inflation to fall to 18 percent in 1997 from about 23 percent this year.
